title: Expense Policy
text: This policy defines the general process and rules for submitting and reimbursing business expenses. Travel-related expenses have their own specific limits and are governed by the Travel Policy, which takes precedence over this policy wherever the two differ.

title: Expense Policy
text: Expenses must be reasonable, business-related, and incurred in the course of performing job duties.

title: Expense Policy
text: A receipt is required for any expense over $25. Expenses without a required receipt will not be reimbursed.

title: Expense Policy
text: Expenses must be submitted within 30 days of being incurred.

title: Expense Policy
text: All expenses require direct manager approval before reimbursement is processed.

title: Expense Policy
text: Approved expenses are reimbursed within 10 business days of approval, via the standard payroll reimbursement cycle.

title: Expense Policy
text:
- Travel-related expenses (flights, hotels, meals while traveling): see the Travel Policy for specific dollar caps.
- Equipment purchases: see the Procurement Policy for approval thresholds.

title: Procurement Policy
text: This policy defines the approval thresholds required to purchase goods or services on behalf of Nexora Technologies, including equipment such as laptops. It does not define equipment eligibility or specifications — see the Device Policy for that.

title: Procurement Policy
text: May be approved directly by the requesting employee's manager.

title: Procurement Policy
text: Require department head approval in addition to manager approval.

title: Procurement Policy
text: Require Finance approval in addition to department head approval.

title: Procurement Policy
text: Laptop and equipment purchases follow the thresholds in Section 2, based on the total cost of the configuration requested. See the Device Policy for standard configurations and who is eligible to request equipment.

title: Procurement Policy
text: Purchases over $5,000 must use a vendor from the approved vendor list maintained by Finance, unless an exception is granted.

title: Procurement Policy
text: All approved purchase requests must be logged in the procurement system with the approving manager, department head, or Finance approver recorded.

title: Travel Policy
text: This policy defines rules and limits specific to business travel expenses. It supplements the Expense Policy; where the two conflict on travel-specific limits, this policy governs.

title: Travel Policy
text: All business travel must be approved by a direct manager in advance of booking.

title: Travel Policy
text:
- Domestic flights: reimbursed up to a maximum of $600 per round trip, economy class.
- International flights: reimbursed up to a maximum of $2,500 per round trip, economy or premium economy class.

title: Travel Policy
text:
- Domestic hotel stays: up to $200 per night.
- International hotel stays: up to $300 per night.

title: Travel Policy
text: Meal expenses while traveling are reimbursed up to $75 per day, itemized receipts required for any single meal over $25.

title: Travel Policy
text: Travel expenses follow the same submission window and receipt requirements as the general Expense Policy (30-day submission window, receipts required over $25), but are subject to the caps in Section 3 above rather than the Expense Policy's general limits.

title: Attendance Policy
text: This policy defines expectations around working hours, attendance tracking, and leave due to illness. It does not cover annual (vacation) leave — see the Leave Policy for that.

title: Attendance Policy
text: Employees are expected to be available during core hours of 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM local time, regardless of whether they are working on-site or remotely.

title: Attendance Policy
text: On-site employees log attendance via the office badge system.

title: Attendance Policy
text: Employees working remotely under the Remote Work Policy log attendance via the internal time-tracking system rather than badge access. This is a tracking mechanism only and does not affect eligibility to work remotely, which is governed separately by the Remote Work Policy.

title: Attendance Policy
text: An employee who needs to take leave due to illness must notify their manager before the start of the workday, or as soon as reasonably possible.

title: Attendance Policy
text: Illness-related leave of 3 or more consecutive days requires a medical certificate submitted to HR. This leave is tracked separately from, and does not draw down, an employee's annual leave balance under the Leave Policy.

title: Attendance Policy
text: Repeated unplanned absences without notification may result in disciplinary action per the Code of Conduct.

title: Benefits Policy
text: This policy describes health and supplementary benefits available to eligible employees of Nexora Technologies. It does not cover annual leave — see the Leave Policy for that.

title: Benefits Policy
text: Full-time employees are eligible for health insurance coverage beginning after a 90-day probationary period.

title: Benefits Policy
text: Part-time employees receive prorated benefits coverage based on contracted hours, beginning after the same 90-day probationary period.

title: Benefits Policy
text: Contractors are **not** eligible for any benefits described in this policy. See the Contractor Policy for the full list of benefits contractors do and do not receive.

title: Benefits Policy
text: Eligible employees receive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Premiums are partially subsidized by Nexora Technologies according to the current benefits schedule maintained by HR.

title: Benefits Policy
text: Eligible full-time employees receive a company retirement contribution matching up to 4% of base salary.

title: Benefits Policy
text: Benefits enrollment occurs within 30 days of eligibility start, or during the annual open enrollment period.

title: Contractor Policy
text: This policy defines which company policies and benefits apply to independent contractors engaged by Nexora Technologies, as distinct from full-time and part-time employees.

title: Contractor Policy
text: This policy applies to all individuals engaged under a contractor agreement, regardless of engagement length.

title: Contractor Policy
text: Contractors are **not** eligible for annual leave benefits under the Leave Policy. Time off for contractors is governed solely by the terms of the individual's contractor agreement.

title: Contractor Policy
text: Contractors are **not** eligible for health insurance or other benefits described in the Benefits Policy.

title: Contractor Policy
text: Contractors may be issued standard equipment under the Device Policy, subject to department head approval and the approval thresholds defined in the Procurement Policy.

title: Contractor Policy
text: Contractors remain subject to the Code of Conduct, the Conflict of Interest Policy, and the Acceptable Use Policy for the duration of their engagement, even though they are excluded from the leave and benefits policies above.

title: Contractor Policy
text: Contractor engagement terms, compensation, and termination conditions are governed by the individual's signed contractor agreement, not by this policy.

title: Employee Handbook
text: Welcome to Nexora Technologies. This handbook provides a general overview of employment policies. For authoritative, current details on any specific topic, always refer to the dedicated policy document — this handbook is a summary and is not updated as frequently as individual policies.

title: Employee Handbook
text: Nexora Technologies employs full-time employees, part-time employees, and contractors. Benefits and entitlements differ by employment type; see the Contractor Policy and Benefits Policy for details.

title: Employee Handbook
text: Standard working hours are 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM local time, Monday through Friday, with a one-hour lunch break. Flexible scheduling may be arranged with manager approval.

title: Employee Handbook
text: Full-time employees are entitled to 18 days of paid annual leave per year. See the Leave Policy for accrual rules, carryover limits, and eligibility details.

title: Employee Handbook
text: Employees who are unable to work due to illness should notify their manager as soon as possible. See the Attendance Policy for details on medical leave.

title: Employee Handbook
text: All employees are expected to comply with the Code of Conduct and the Conflict of Interest Policy. Violations may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.

title: Employee Handbook
text: Employees are issued standard equipment on their first day. See the Device Policy and Acceptable Use Policy for details on equipment eligibility and acceptable use of company systems.

title: Employee Handbook
text: For questions not answered by this handbook, contact HR directly or consult the specific policy document relevant to your question.

title: Leave Policy
text: > **This version is archived and no longer in effect.** It applied from 2025-01-01 until superseded by Leave Policy v3.0 on 2026-07-01.

title: Leave Policy
text: This policy defines annual (vacation) leave entitlements for eligible employees of Nexora Technologies.

title: Leave Policy
text: Full-time employees accrue annual leave at a rate that totals 18 days per calendar year.

title: Leave Policy
text: Part-time employees accrue annual leave on a pro-rated basis according to their contracted hours.

title: Leave Policy
text: Leave accrues monthly, at a rate of 1.5 days per month.

title: Leave Policy
text: Unused annual leave does not carry over to the following calendar year. Any unused balance is forfeited on December 31.

title: Leave Policy
text: Leave requests must be submitted to a direct manager at least 5 business days in advance for approval.

title: Leave Policy
text: This policy defines annual (vacation) leave entitlements for eligible employees of Nexora Technologies. This version supersedes Leave Policy v2.0 effective 2026-07-01.

title: Leave Policy
text: Full-time employees receive 20 annual leave days per calendar year, granted as a lump sum at the start of the year.

title: Leave Policy
text: Part-time employees receive annual leave on a pro-rated basis according to their contracted hours.

title: Leave Policy
text: Contractors are not eligible for annual leave under this policy. See the Contractor Policy for the full list of benefits contractors do and do not receive.

title: Leave Policy
text: Unlike the prior version of this policy, leave is granted as a full-year lump sum rather than monthly accrual.

title: Leave Policy
text: Up to 5 unused annual leave days may be carried over into the following calendar year. Any balance beyond 5 days is forfeited on December 31.

title: Leave Policy
text: Leave requests must be submitted to a direct manager at least 5 business days in advance for approval.

title: Leave Policy
text:
- Annual leave entitlement increased from 18 to 20 days.
- Accrual method changed from monthly accrual to an upfront annual lump sum.
- Carryover introduced: up to 5 days may now roll over (v2.0 allowed no carryover).

title: Remote Work Policy
text: > **This version is archived and no longer in effect.** It applied from 2024-01-01 until superseded by Remote Work Policy v2.0 on 2025-03-01.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: This policy governs where employees may perform their work.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: Employees may work remotely within their home country with manager approval, on either a full-time or hybrid basis.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: International remote work is **not permitted** under this policy. All employees must perform work from within their country of employment.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: Employees working remotely must use company-issued equipment and connect to internal systems only via the VPN described in the Acceptable Use Policy.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: > **This version is archived and no longer in effect.** It applied from 2025-03-01 until superseded by Remote Work Policy v3.0 on 2026-07-01.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: This policy governs where employees may perform their work.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: Employees may work remotely within their home country with manager approval, on either a full-time or hybrid basis.

title: Remote Work Policy
text:
Unlike the prior version of this policy, international remote work is now permitted, subject to the following conditions:

- Maximum of 30 consecutive days per calendar year in any single country.
- Requires written manager approval submitted at least 2 weeks in advance.
- Employee remains responsible for any personal tax or visa implications.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: Employees working remotely, domestically or internationally, must use company-issued equipment and connect to internal systems only via the VPN described in the Acceptable Use Policy.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: - International remote work is now permitted (previously prohibited entirely), capped at 30 days/year with manager approval only.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: This policy governs where employees may perform their work. This version supersedes Remote Work Policy v2.0 effective 2026-07-01.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: Employees may work remotely within their home country with manager approval, on either a full-time or hybrid basis.

title: Remote Work Policy
text:
Employees may work internationally under the following conditions:

- Maximum of 90 days per calendar year, consecutive or cumulative, in any single country.
- Requires written approval from the employee's manager **and** HR **and** Legal, submitted at least 4 weeks in advance.
- Employee must file a Cross-Border Work Notification with HR prior to departure, covering tax, payroll, and immigration considerations.
- Employee remains responsible for any personal tax or visa implications not covered by the notification review.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: Employees working remotely, domestically or internationally, must use company-issued equipment and connect to internal systems only via the VPN described in the Acceptable Use Policy.

title: Remote Work Policy
text:
- International remote work cap increased from 30 to 90 days per calendar year.
- Approval now requires HR and Legal sign-off in addition to manager approval (previously manager approval only).
- A new Cross-Border Work Notification filing is now required prior to international remote work.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
text: This policy defines acceptable use of Nexora Technologies' IT systems, including remote access to internal systems. This is distinct from the Remote Work Policy, which governs where an employee physically performs their work — this policy governs how systems are accessed regardless of work location.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
text: Remote access to internal systems (email, source code repositories, internal tools) is permitted only via the company-managed VPN, from a company-issued device.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
text: All remote access requires multi-factor authentication as described in the Password Policy.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
text:
- Sharing account credentials with another person.
- Installing unauthorized software on company-issued devices.
- Using company systems for activity that violates the Code of Conduct.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
text: Nexora Technologies reserves the right to monitor use of company systems for security and compliance purposes, in accordance with applicable law.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
text: Violations of this policy may result in suspension of system access and disciplinary action under the Code of Conduct.

title: Device Policy
text: This policy defines who is eligible to receive company equipment and what standard configurations are available. It does not define purchase approval thresholds — see the Procurement Policy for that.

title: Device Policy
text: All full-time employees are issued a standard laptop on their first day of employment at no additional approval required beyond onboarding.

title: Device Policy
text: Contractors may be issued a laptop only with department head approval. The purchase or issuance still follows the dollar-based approval thresholds defined in the Procurement Policy.

title: Device Policy
text: Nexora Technologies offers two standard laptop configurations: a standard configuration (under $1,000) and a performance configuration (over $1,000, primarily for engineering roles). Requests for the performance configuration therefore trigger the department head approval threshold defined in the Procurement Policy.

title: Device Policy
text: Equipment replacement due to damage or end-of-life follows the same eligibility rules as initial issuance. Upgrade requests above $1,000 require department head approval per the Procurement Policy; requests above $5,000 additionally require Finance approval.

title: Device Policy
text: All company-issued equipment must be returned upon termination of employment or contractor engagement.

title: Password Policy
text: This policy defines minimum password and authentication requirements for all Nexora Technologies accounts.

title: Password Policy
text:
- Minimum length of 14 characters.
- Must not reuse any of the previous 10 passwords.
- Must be changed every 180 days.

title: Password Policy
text: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is required for all accounts with access to internal systems, including VPN access described in the Acceptable Use Policy.

title: Password Policy
text: Employees must use the company-approved password manager. Storing passwords in plaintext files or browsers without the approved password manager is prohibited.

title: Password Policy
text: Any suspected compromise of account credentials must be reported to IT Security immediately.

title: Code of Conduct
text: This policy sets out the standards of conduct expected of everyone working at or on behalf of Nexora Technologies, including employees and contractors.

title: Code of Conduct
text: Employees must act honestly and in the company's best interest in all business dealings.

title: Code of Conduct
text: Employees must treat colleagues, customers, and partners with respect. Harassment or discrimination of any kind will not be tolerated.

title: Code of Conduct
text: Employees must protect confidential company and customer information, consistent with the data-handling expectations described in this section (Nexora Technologies does not currently maintain a separate standalone Data Privacy Policy document; data-handling obligations are covered here and in the Acceptable Use Policy).

title: Code of Conduct
text: Employees must disclose any potential conflict of interest. See the Conflict of Interest Policy for the full disclosure process.

title: Code of Conduct
text: Suspected violations of this Code of Conduct should be reported to HR or through the anonymous ethics reporting channel.

title: Code of Conduct
text: Violations may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or contractor engagement.

title: Conflict of Interest Policy
text: This policy defines what constitutes a conflict of interest and the process for disclosing one, supplementing the general expectations in the Code of Conduct.

title: Conflict of Interest Policy
text: A conflict of interest arises when an employee's personal interests could improperly influence, or appear to influence, their professional judgment or decisions on behalf of Nexora Technologies.

title: Conflict of Interest Policy
text: Employees must disclose any outside employment or consulting arrangement, particularly with a competitor, customer, or supplier, before accepting it.

title: Conflict of Interest Policy
text: Gifts from vendors, customers, or partners with a value under $100 may be accepted without disclosure.

title: Conflict of Interest Policy
text: Gifts valued at $100 or more must be disclosed to a manager and may need to be declined or surrendered to the company.

title: Conflict of Interest Policy
text: Conflicts must be disclosed in writing to HR or the employee's manager as soon as they are identified, using the conflict disclosure form.

title: Conflict of Interest Policy
text: Failure to disclose a known conflict of interest is treated as a violation of the Code of Conduct.
